newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea food crisis worsening -- U.S. envoy.
newsitem.headline: North Korea food crisis worsening -- U.S. envoy.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador to the United Nations said on Friday that North Korea's food crisis is getting worse but Washington has no evidence to back up reports that Pyongyang is diverting international aid to its military.

Bill Richardson, who made several visits to North Korea prior to becoming ambassador to the United Nations earlier this year, said the United States was likely to respond to any further appeals for food aid to North Korea.
"We think the situation is getting worse," Richardson told reporters in Tokyo.
"We're ready to entertain other requests through the World Food Programme, based on humanitarian needs," he said.

Richardson is in Tokyo on a two-week, 10-nation tour mainly to lobby for reform of the United Nations, including admitting Japan as a permanent member of the Security Council and a broadening of the UN's financial base.

The United States, a major food donor to North Korea, has provided $52 million this year through the U.N. World Food Programme to help stave off a famine caused by two years of disastrous floods compounded now by a drought.

Members of a U.S. congressional delegation just back in Washington from visiting the secretive Stalinist North Korea, have said they saw evidence that food aid may have wound up on the plates of North Korea's military.
"We right now, on the reports that food is being diverted to the military, are looking into the reports. We can't verify them," Richardson said.
He said U.S. food aid was targeted mainly at North Korean children under the age of six and "we believe it is getting to them".

Richardson gave an optimistic assessment of talks between the two Koreas, the United States and China to arrange formal negotiations aimed at setting up a permanent peace mechanism on the Korean peninsula.
Senior officials from the four countries have failed to set an agenda for the formal peace talks but agreed to meet again on September 15 in New York.
"The tone, the atmospherics of the talks was good," Richardson said. "In the next round we get down to the nitty gritty of logistics."
